inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back ShareBasedCompensation $153M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $56M (SEC XBRL companyfacts); WTW publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 92.87M basic on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-27) plus ~0.6M dilutive RSU/PSU (Q2-26 diluted weighted 94M vs basic gap); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. WTW is a heavy repurchaser ($1.65B FY2025, $750M H1-2026), so the flat count is funded, with surplus buyback beyond SBC being value-neutral capital return
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), beta ~0.8 (broker/consultant, low-cyclicality fee revenue), ERP 5.0% -> CoE ~8.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (IG senior notes), ~3.9% after tax; debt ~19% of EV at market. Arithmetic WACC ~7.4%; rounded UP to 8.0% to reflect the soft-P&C-pricing exposure in Risk & Broking and AI-substitution risk in consulting. Same WACC in all scenarios: risk is carried by the probability-weighted scenarios, not a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost ($122M FY2025) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. One treatment (lease cost in flows), never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Small NCI ($82M book at 2026-06-30; $8M FY2025 NCI earnings) deducted once in the equity bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'). WTW is an asset-light broker/consultant that earns fees and commissions and does not underwrite risk, so it is not routed to the insurer BVPS model; fiduciary cash/receivables held for clients are excluded from cash and from net debt (they are offset by fiduciary liabilities). FY0 = FY2025 continuing basis (TRANZACT sold 31-Dec-2024, so FY2025 revenue $9,708M is ex-TRANZACT). NORMALIZATION: FY2024 GAAP net loss (-$98M) and 6.3% operating margin are distorted by the one-off TRANZACT ~$1.0B goodwill impairment + $1.1B loss on disposal (~$2.1B pretax, non-cash) and are NOT used as an earnings-power anchor; projections anchor to FY2025 (adjusted operating margin 25.2%, GAAP op margin 23.0%, reported FCF $1,546M = 15.9%) and the Propel 2028 target. EBITDA margin in the drivers is a CASH-EBITDA margin pre-SBC: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA (adj OI ~$2,446M + depreciation $226M) is ~27.5% after SBC / ~29.1% pre-SBC, but FY2025 OCF ran ~$300M below adjusted NI + D&A + SBC (pension contributions, deferred-comp and E&O cash, working capital), so the component build is calibrated to reproduce FY2025 owner FCF (~15.8% unlevered) at a ~24.5% cash-EBITDA margin. 2026-28 margins carry Propel's ~$625M implementation cash cost (~1.5-2pp/yr) offsetting underlying expansion; post-2028 margins step up as ~$350M net run-rate savings land (management's ~30% adjusted operating margin target is NOT assumed in base - base matures at 27.5% cash EBITDA, ~+3pp vs FY2025). Revenue: FY2026 +8% (H1-26 +8.8% reported; ~5% organic + Newfront/FlowStone/Al-Futtaim Willis consolidation + FX), then mid-single-digit organic decaying to 3.5%. D&A includes acquired-intangible amortization (~$192M FY2025, rising post-Newfront) because it is largely tax-deductible; it rolls off gradually. Working capital: brokerage/consulting receivables grow with revenue, so wc_capture is negative (-10% of the revenue increase). Interest income not stripped: WTW is net debt, not net cash. Buybacks: $1.65B FY2025 ($56M withholding), $750M H1-2026; buybacks exceed SBC so the flat count is funded. EQUITY BRIDGE: the year-1 flow is full FY2026, but net debt is struck at 30-Jun-2026, which already contains H1-2026 cash generation (reported FCF $360M + after-tax interest ~$121M - equity-award withholding $57M - SBC funding ~$109M ~= $315M unlevered owner FCF); that $315M is deducted so it is not counted twice. Newfront ($1.3B, Jan-2026) and FlowStone (Apr-2026) acquisition cash is already in the 30-Jun-2026 net debt and their revenue is in the FY2026 growth step. DB pension schemes (net position not modelled; historically near-funded/in surplus on the UK plans) are excluded from the bridge - a modest conservative omission if in surplus.

equity_bridge.item: H1-2026 owner FCF already in 30-Jun-2026 net debt
equity_bridge.note: Y1 flow is full-year FY2026; H1 reported FCF $360M + after-tax interest ~$121M - withholding $57M - SBC $109M; removes the half-year double count

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic revenue growth (FY2025 5% organic; FY2026 guidance mid-single-digit organic) -- book-value CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-7.3% 3yr, -5.9% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+3.1%/+2.4%) and EPS (+22%/+16%) CAGRs. Book value shrinks because WTW returns more than 100% of earnings via buybacks ($1.0-3.5B/yr since 2021, incl. the $1B Aon break fee) and took the ~$2.1B TRANZACT write-down in FY2024 - it is not a measure of business growth. Reported revenue CAGRs are depressed by the TRANZACT divestiture (FY2025 ex-TRANZACT vs FY2020/22 incl.) and EPS CAGRs are flattered by buybacks plus the FY2024 GAAP loss base; organic growth (~5%) is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding: FY2018 $940M, FY2023 $952M, FY2025 $1,337M. FY2019-22 capex is missing from the XBRL-derived CSV so 3yr/5yr owner-FCF CAGRs are not computable; the 7yr (FY2018-25) owner-FCF CAGR is 5.2% and the 2yr (FY2023-25) 18.5% reflects transformation-programme savings and the end of its cash costs. SBC ($125M->$153M) grew slower than FCF, so no SBC-outgrowing-cash-flow warning.

base.narrative: Mid-single-digit organic growth holds through a softening P&C cycle; Propel delivers most of its savings but cash EBITDA matures ~3pp above FY2025, short of the ~30% adjusted-OI target.

bull.narrative: Propel hits the ~30% adjusted margin in 2028 and holds; Newfront scales US middle-market broking and FlowStone wealth/private markets add a growth leg; organic 6%+.

bear.narrative: Soft commercial P&C and reinsurance pricing plus payroll softness cut organic growth to ~3%; Propel savings are competed away / reinvested and AI erodes consulting fee pools, leaving cash margins stuck near FY2025.

scenario_narratives.base: WTW compounds organic revenue at ~5% (benefits/retirement advisory demand from ageing populations and regulatory complexity in HWC, new business and retention in R&B) while the commercial P&C rate cycle softens, with Newfront, FlowStone and the Al-Futtaim Willis buy-in adding ~3pp in FY2026. Propel's ~$625M cash cost depresses 2026-28 cash margins by ~1.5-2pp before ~$350M net run-rate savings lift cash EBITDA to ~27.5% pre-SBC (about +3pp on FY2025), below management's ~30% adjusted-operating-margin ambition. Capital returns continue at ~100% of FCF; the share count is held flat with SBC expensed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Propel is the transformation programme repeated: WTW reaches the ~30% adjusted operating margin in 2028 and closes the margin gap to Aon, the broking platform gains share in US middle market and specialty through Newfront, and FlowStone gives the Wealth/investments business a private-markets growth leg. Organic growth runs 6-7% early, decaying to 4%; cash EBITDA matures at 29.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The P&C and reinsurance pricing cycle turns decisively soft and corporate payroll/benefits budgets tighten, cutting organic growth to ~3%; generative-AI tools commoditise actuarial, benefits and compensation-benchmarking work so Propel savings are passed through to clients rather than retained; Newfront integration disappoints. Cash margins stay near the FY2025 level (~24.5-25%) and terminal growth is 2.5%. The business remains solidly cash generative - this is a de-rating, not a solvency, case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the R&B segment is entering a soft P&C pricing phase and AI substitution of consulting work is a live, unproven-either-way risk; base at 50% as mid-single-digit organic growth is well evidenced (FY2025 5%, H1-26 5% organic); bull trimmed to 30% because it needs Propel to deliver the full 30% margin target AND the acquisitions to integrate cleanly, two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Asset-light fee/commission business valued on unlevered owner FCF (SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, share count flat), anchored on normalized FY2025 earnings power rather than the TRANZACT-distorted FY2024 GAAP loss, with margin expansion credited only partially toward management's Propel target.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the value; an 18x cap on terminal FCF binds near Gordon at 8%/3%
Propel margin delivery: each 1pp of mature cash-EBITDA margin is worth roughly $8-9/share
Soft P&C pricing cycle compressing R&B commission growth
AI substitution in actuarial/benefits consulting fee pools
Non-adjusted cash leakage (pensions, E&O, deferred comp) has historically kept FCF well below adjusted earnings - the calibration assumes it persists
Integration of Newfront ($1.3B) and FlowStone; debt-funded M&A raised net debt to $4.9B
